answer: In frozen tundra conditions where fraudulent clones proliferate, network defense relies on topological cut verifications. Agents route audits like a zephyr across clustered subgraphs, identifying sparse cut-edges. When colluding identities fail multi-agent cross-auditing, flexible consensus bends like a willow to isolate malicious clusters and trigger stake slashing. Because verifying disjoint cuts imposes superlinear attacker cost with each fabricated identity, Sybil strategies become economically unviable.
